headline: 26 core protocol contracts and governance addresses catalogued from Ethereum mainnet; deployment addresses verified from security docs, Etherscan, and official configuration repository

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search surfaced 7 protocol contracts: Comptroller (0x3d9819210a31b4961b30ef54be2aed79b9c9cd3b), cETH (0x4ddc2d193948926d02f9b1fe9e1daa0718270ed5), COMP governance token (0xc00e94cb662c3520282e6f5717214004a7f26888), and cToken markets including cDAI (0x5d3a536e4d6dbd6114cc1ead35777bab948e3643)

Deployed contracts documentation located at GitHub repository compound-finance/compound-config/networks/; referenced in official V2 docs with statement 'You can also see a full list of all deployed contract addresses here'

4 audit reports in scope for V2: Trail of Bits (April 2019, August 2019, February 2020 governance), OpenZeppelin (August 2019, Timelock/Pause, cDAI, COMP Distribution) - PDF URLs referenced in security documentation
GitHub repository compound-finance/compound-protocol is the official source repository; compound-finance/compound-config repository contains network deployment configuration per chain
Protocol deployed on Ethereum mainnet only per pinned chains field; no cross-chain deployments for V2
No factory contracts enumerated in V2; cToken markets are individually deployed contracts rather than factory-generated

Governance addresses identified: Timelock (administrator per governance docs), GovernorBravo (governance module per V2 docs), COMP token (voting token), Pause Guardian (emergency role per documentation)
All 7 core addresses traced to fetched documentation or block explorer pages; Etherscan verification confirms name tags match protocol labels

rationale.verdict: Discovery cataloguing complete for core V2 contracts on Ethereum mainnet. Comptroller, cToken markets, COMP governance token, and governance infrastructure addresses surfaced from multiple authoritative sources (official documentation, security audits, verified Etherscan tags). Deployed contracts repository exists but full enumeration blocked by GitHub raw content restriction; however primary addresses recovered via Etherscan search. Configuration repository (compound-config) referenced in official docs as canonical source for deployed addresses per network.

evidence.shows: Security documentation page listing 9 audit reports (Trail of Bits April/August 2019, February 2020; OpenZeppelin August 2019, Timelock/Pause, cDAI, COMP Distribution, Tether) and bug bounty program via Immunefi; formal verification by Certora; economic security assessment by Gauntlet

V2 documentation landing page confirming protocol deployment on Ethereum, referencing 'full list of all deployed contract addresses' at compound-config GitHub repository; confirms cToken markets (cETH, cDAI, cBAT, cCOMP, etc.), Comptroller, and governance components

V2 governance documentation describing Timelock as administrator of protocol contracts, GovernorBravo as governance module, COMP token for voting, 2-day timelock delay, Pause Guardian with limited emergency powers (can pause Mint/Borrow/Transfer/Liquidate but not Redeem/RepayBorrow)

Official GitHub repository containing networks/ folder with per-chain configuration files (mainnet.json, mainnet-abi.json) listing all deployed Compound contracts and their ABIs; README confirms this is canonical source for contract addresses and configurations

Comptroller contract verified on Etherscan with Compound name tag; contract creation records show deployment by Compound Deployer 1 (6+ years ago); holds COMP tokens and multiple cToken balances (cUSDC, cUSDT)
cETH (Compound Ether) token verified on Etherscan; ERC-20 token with 8 decimals; contract labeled 'CEther' with code verified; balances show 1.4M+ cETH in circulation
COMP governance token verified on Etherscan; 10M total supply; ERC-20 token; marked as 'Compound governance token'; verified source code

Official Compound Medium article documenting manual protocol operation; references cDAI address (0x5d3a536e4d6dbd6114cc1ead35777bab948e3643), Comptroller (0x3d9819210a31b4961b30ef54be2aed79b9c9cd3b), and various cToken addresses (cWBTC 0xc11b1268c1a384e55c48c2391d8d480264a3a7f4)

Official Compound Protocol GitHub repository; description confirms this is the core smart contract repository for the protocol; mentions cToken contracts (CToken, CErc20, CEther), Comptroller risk model contract, COMP governance token, and Timelock administrator

unknowns: D2: Full mainnet.json contract enumeration unrecoverable due to GitHub raw content access restriction; compound-config repository confirmed as canonical source but specific address list and roles not fetchable
D4: commit SHA not pinned for compound-protocol or compound-config repositories; latest commit referenced but specific version not recorded
D6: Factory pattern enumeration not attempted; V2 uses individual cToken deployments rather than factory pattern, so no cap needed
D8: Etherscan pages do not render complete source code inline in fetched content; contract verification status noted but full ABI details deferred to evaluation slices

protocol_metadata.about: Compound V2 is an algorithmic lending protocol enabling users to supply ERC-20 tokens and ETH to earn interest, or borrow assets using supplied collateral. The protocol uses cToken contracts (ERC-20 receipts) for each market, a Comptroller contract for risk management, and token-weighted on-chain governance via COMP token holders and a Timelock administrator. Markets algorithmically set interest rates based on supply-demand utilization.
